MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 28, 2022
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Bucknum
at 5:00 p.m., on June 28, 2022, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on June 23, 2022, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at
the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Raths
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CONSIDERATION OF ADDITION OF LATE ARISING MATTER

City Attorney Curley announced that the City was delivered an application for a temporary
restraining order (TRO) from Mr. Schlesinger putting a control on terms the Council could set in
the future for the 2022 Election. It just came in this afternoon, we have not had an opportunity to
agendize or post it. The Hearing is tomorrow morning at 8:30 a.m. so we have ticked the box on
needing to respond and there will need to be a 4/5’s vote to add to tonight’s Closed Session.

Motion made by Council Member Kelly, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs to add this item to
Closed Session.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
City Council Minutes  1  June 28, 2022
 AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel: Existing Litigation Paragraph (1) of Subdivision (d) of
  Section 54956.9. Schlesinger v. City of Mission Viejo: 30-2022-01253878-CU-WM-CJC

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Stated her disappointment that this morning no Council Members
  attended Hearing this morning. She outlined the hearing this morning and criticized the City
  Attorney and questioned the City Council on when they knew cumulative voting would not
  legal for general law cities.

  Michael Schlesinger, M.V: Addressed the Council regarding his lawsuit against the City. He
  stated that the motion by Judge Shwarm ruled that Goodell and Kelley have to run for election.
  He criticized the slap lawsuit the City filed against him. He trusts that the City will do
  something reasonable so that Judge Shwarm will not have to issue another opinion to secure
  his voting rights.

CS2. Conference with Labor Negotiators: Agency Designated Representatives: Dennis
  Wilberg, Cheryl Dyas, Monique Goetz, Peter Brown Esq, and William P. Curley III.
  Employee Organization: Animal Services Department; SEIU Organizing Staff.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Questioned what is going on between the City and SEIU. She stated
  that if this is being pushed by one of the contract cities using the Animal Shelter, she
  recommends canceling the contract with that city and offer them a rental contract for space
  and they can hire their own employees.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:09 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:03 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Curley reported on the litigation matters for CS1 and the added CS3 on the TRO
motion, that Council gave direction and instruction but no reportable actions occurred under the
statute. CS2 was a personnel matter that will be reported on a later item this evening.

INVOCATION: Council Member Goodell

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

PRESENTATIONS

City Council Minutes  2  June 28, 2022
 P1. Proclaim July 2022 as Parks and Recreation Month

  Mayor Bucknum presented proclamation to Recreation and Community Services Director
  Mark Nix.

P2. 2022 Drought Update by Santa Margarita and Moulton Niguel Water Districts

  Received presentations from Director of External Affairs Jim Leach of Santa Margarita
  Water District and Assistant General Manager Matt Collings of Moulton Niguel Water
  District.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Michael Schlesinger, M.V: Addressed the Council regarding his lawsuit against the City. He stated
that the motion by Judge Shwarm ruled that Goodell and Kelley have to run for election. He
criticized the slap lawsuit the City filed against him. He trusts that the City will do something
reasonable so that Judge Shwarm will not have to issue another opinion to secure his voting rights.

Virginia Payne, M.V.: Spoke out about the influx of the homeless population and voiced her
concerns.

Gabriel El Mahrek, M.V.: Spoke against the LGBTQ community and suggested a boycott on those
companies that support the LGBTQ community.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: Addressed the Council regarding the street sweeping contract and outlined the
Waste Management contract that now includes street sweeping. He reminded the Council that this
is a public service position not a full-time job and recapped Council Member Raths proposal of a
stipend increase in 2018.

Ed Maurer, M.V.: He addressed item #13 on the Consent Calendar regarding four replacement
vehicles and hopes that these are electric trucks. Spoke on the Orange County Power Authority
and the problems they are having.

Louise Adler, Lake Forest: Stated that she attended the hearing this morning and clarified that the
rumor about yelling in the court room and hallway is inaccurate.

Cathy Palmer, M.V.: Questioned the Council on why it took a Superior Court Judge’s decision to
make sure the City Council adhere to the rule of law and stand for election when their terms expire.
Criticized the City Attorney for suggesting at the hearing that to stagger terms some districts should
be six-year terms and some four rather than two and four. She stated the court ruled that it had not
agreed to extend any Council Member terms and it could not have done so and asked for an apology
from the City Council.

Walt Lawson, M.V.: He recapped the court hearing events from this morning. Questioned the
illegal term extensions of Mayor Bucknum, Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, and Council Member Raths, to
which, City Attorney Bill Curley has never answered his questions. Accused Council Member’s
Goodell and Kelly for remaining silent when asked why their terms should be extended. Suggested
City Council Minutes  3  June 28, 2022
 that Mr. Curley and his firm to refund the City for all the work on this case especially the frivolous
filings.

Carlos Pianelli, M.V.: Spoke on the U.S. Constitution and to have the moral courage to stand up
for what is right.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Recapped on the court hearing this morning. Stated that this community owes
gratitude Michael Schlesinger who was served with an anti-slap suit which was mean spirited and
the judge ruled that it was frivolous. She expressed that is has taken four and half years to right a
wrong. She asked that the City Council do the right thing and apologize.

Tom Moore, M.V.: Spoke on the CVS building and the little affect not purchasing the building for
the Core Area Vision Plan. Encouraged the involvement of property owners and praised Council
Member Goodell on his vote to purchase the building.

City Attorney Curley explained in court today Mr. Schlesinger and his Lawyers attempted to graft
into the Injunction a decision on the Writ. This was pointed this out to the Judge. The Judge said
it was an error and took it out. The Judge did not buy their position that the Writ should be decided
on. The Writ is scheduled in the future. The Writ can role back the three versus five, that is by no
means certain and is not a given in any stretch on any law in California or anywhere. This is an
undecided decision. What the Court did with the Injunction, we thought was fair so we didn’t
oppose it. With the Writ it could go five district or back to three districts. It’s fair to give people
notice. We will be Calling the Election at the next City Council Meeting and the Injunction is a
placeholder until the Writ is decided so nothing is certain. He stated in litigation you put forth a
variety of defenses, some are strong some are not. This will not be resolved for a month or two.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  5  June 28, 2022
   2021-22 capital improvement project 327 for the District 5 Regional Bikeways - Mission

13. Lease Agreement for Four (4) Public Services Replacement Vehicles

14. Janitorial Supplies at City Facilities

  Authorized staff to issue a purchase order for Waxie Sanitary Supply for Janitorial Supplies

  Awarded contract to OC Concrete, LLC, (A22-24) for the Maintenance and Repairs to the

City Council Minutes  6  June 28, 2022
 PUBLIC HEARINGS

18. Oso Creek Golf Course and Recreation and Community Services User Fees

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas gave the staff report.

  Council Member Goodell ask staff to look into resident rates versus non-resident rates for
  green fees.

  Mayor Bucknum opened the Public Hearing at 7:34 pm.

  With no public input the Mayor Bucknum closed the Public Hearing at 7:34 pm.

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs agreed with Council Member Goodell to take a look at resident rates
  versus non-resident rates.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to direct
  staff to review all options on how the City manages the golf course going forward.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Sachs
  NOES:  Raths
  ABSENT: None

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt
  Resolution 22-21 Amending Current Fees and Establishing New Fees for the Oso Creek Golf
  Course and Recreation and Community Services Programs.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Sachs
  NOES:  Raths
  ABSENT:  None

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

22. Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Received report from Council Member Raths.

23. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) Report

  Received report from Council Member Goodell.

24. Transportation Corridor Agency (TCA) Report

  Received report from Council Member Kelley.
City Council Minutes  8  June 28, 2022
 CITY MANAGER REPORT

25. Parks and Facilities Improvement Projects Update

  Received presentation Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

26. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell had no comments.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley the Amateur Radio Operators Field Day this past Saturday and she gave a
shout out to resident Charlie Speelman. She stated that the participants thanked the City for going
out of the way to accommodate this event. She announced the Fourth of July Street Faire coming
up and the Mission Viejo Library Summer Reading Program. Council Member Kelley read from
an article on Mission Viejo receiving he honor of being named one of the ten safest cities in
California for 2022. Safewise Team released the report and Mission Viejo was ranked eighth. She
indicated last year Mission Viejo was named the best City in California to live by 24/7 Wall Street
and also last year Money Magazine rated Mission Viejo as one of the 50 best cities to live in
America. She thanked her Council Colleagues, City Staff and Police Services.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths commented on the election process and apologized on how long it has taken.
Stated that when he was on an ad hoc committee with Council Member Kelley they recommended
to move to district voting and Council Member Sachs suggested looking into rank choice voting
and it’s been another two years and he believes it should have never taken this long. He stated that
he does have a third term if he decides to run again.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs pointed out that government is not in the business for a return on investment
and explained we would not have a Library, Animal Services, Police and Fire Departments if that
was the case. The budgets we look over and manage regarding recreation centers and the programs
we provide require $6.8 million subsidy from the general fund in order to have these things. He
pointed out on the public comment on the plea for Community Energy and he stated that OCPA is
going through more than just a little problem. There was an outcry when the OCPA Board voted
City Council Minutes  9  June 28, 2022
 to charge customers higher rates than they currently pay for electricity provided by Southern
California Edison. He stated that much of OCPA’s power reportedly comes from out of state
windmills and solar panels and the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) is imposing
nearly a two million dollar fine against OCPA for failure to reach resource adequacy. Mayor Pro
Tem Sachs said hat the commercial customers for that agency continue to drop out and the agency’s
projected $42 million loss in it’s first two years now includes the CPUC fine. He announced that
later this week he will be meeting with an individual with the CPUC and will be asking questions
regarding Community Choice Energy and more primarily the demand we have for electric use in
this Country has continued to grow. He stated that the City of Irvine is potentially going to lose
$7.7 million dollars and he thanked City Manager Wilberg and City Attorney Curley who reviewed
the contract for this organization and said we should put a hold on this at this time.

Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum stated that investments in land and real estate has been good for our City. She
gave kudos to the Cultural Arts Committee members for volunteering at the Pacific Symphony
Gala. She read a letter from the Pacific Symphony President John Forsyte thanking the City of
Mission Viejo. Mayor Bucknum announced that the Symphony will be performing on The Village
Green on August 13. She also announced that Shakespeare By the Sea will have a performance of
Much Ado About Nothing at the Community Center on July 20 at 7:00 p.m. Tickets are still
available at www.shakespearebythesea.org. Mayor Bucknum gave an update on the Sober Living
Homes Roundtable has been rescheduled by Senator Bates to be more of a working group to include
other cities in July and then there will be a larger Town Hall in the future.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:06 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, July 12, 2022, at 5:00 p.m.
